commits.subject: reel-native (SMB-REEL-NATIVE-FAULTS, PLR-055): a worker picture above the container-declared size is a worker protocol fault in the host

capabilities_done: host.rs Pool::exchange: every reply FRAME is compared with the container-declared (width, height) (Call.declared, taken from VideoStreamSpec in open_session via WorkerSession.declared) by within_declared_size BEFORE on_frame hands it to reel's route; a larger picture under the reply cap is Failure::Protocol: protocol_faults +1, worker terminated, Av1Error::Worker(Protocol) with the fault slot filled, no picture delivered. Reel's Forward check stays as defence in depth. Smaller pictures stay legal (AV1-ISOBMFF 2.2.4 / Matroska V_AV1 declare the sequence maximum) and a side declared as 0 is not checked. The OversizeFrame (over the reply cap) path is unchanged and still ends as decoder_output_too_large / killed_oversize.

adjacent_not_fixed.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-reel-native/src/host.rs open_session OPEN closure (&mut |_| Err(ReelError::DecoderFault { fault: DecoderFault::Protocol }))
adjacent_not_fixed.text: A FRAME reply to OPEN (the worker answering OPEN with a picture) is refused by this closure through on_frame: the worker is terminated and the call fails with Av1Error::Reel(DecoderFault Protocol) but protocol_faults is not bumped and the fault slot is not set. Same shape as PLR-055 but a different class (an unexpected reply kind, no picture is forwarded to reel); not part of this defect, not covered by a fault variant, left unchanged on purpose (conservative scope, lane SMB-REEL-NATIVE-AV1-WORKER is at 2 failed verdicts). Cheap fix if wanted: guard the Reply::Frame arm of exchange with want == Want::BatchEnd so an OPEN-time frame falls to the existing catch-all Failure::Protocol arm, plus a WorkerTestFault variant that answers OPEN with a FRAME.
